post_title: What cumulative measles death toll (confirmed + suspected) will Bangladesh's DGHS report for 12 November 2026?

question.title: What cumulative measles death toll (confirmed + suspected) will Bangladesh's DGHS report for 12 November 2026?
question.description:
Bangladesh is in the middle of the world's largest measles outbreak of 2026, which began in mid-March 2026 and has run for more than seven months. As of mid-October, WHO's SEARO epidemiological bulletin reported 213,244 suspected and 23,122 laboratory-confirmed cases since 15 March, with 189,484 hospitalisations, and roughly 1,000-1,300 new suspected cases per day since early September "with no steady decline".

DGHS issues a daily measles bulletin covering the 24 hours to 08:00 local time, which Bangladeshi outlets (The Business Standard, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune/UNB, bdnews24, Daily Sun, Sarabangla and others) publish the same afternoon. The bulletin reports a combined cumulative death tally split into laboratory-confirmed measles deaths and suspected measles deaths.

Recent cumulative tolls from those bulletins: 1,162 (11 Oct), 1,186 (16 Oct), 1,189 (17 Oct), 1,204 (20 Oct), 1,205 (21 Oct), 1,207 (22 Oct), 1,214 (23 Oct), 1,222 (24 Oct), 1,233 (26 Oct), 1,240 (27 Oct), 1,242 (28 Oct), 1,249 (29 Oct) and 1,251 (30 Oct), i.e. roughly 4-6 additional deaths per day over the past week. Of the 1,251 total on 30 October, 105 were laboratory-confirmed deaths and about 1,146 were suspected deaths. Cumulative cases passed 250,000 around 30 October, with roughly 1,300 new suspected cases reported per day and about 200,000 measles-related hospital admissions since March.

Response: a nationwide measles-rubella (MR) campaign launched on 26 September 2026 targeting ~3.4 million unvaccinated or missed children, on top of nearly 20 million children vaccinated since April; DGHS reported 21.0 million MR doses administered as of 18 October. Experts (including a late-October AFP-cited review) warn of persistently low full-immunisation coverage (~82%) and vacant vaccinator posts.

The key forecasting judgement is the pace of reported deaths between 30 October and 12 November 2026: whether the recent 4-6 deaths/day persists (implying roughly 1,310-1,330), accelerates as deaths lag the high October case load, or slows as the vaccination campaign and treatment access take effect. Note that DGHS occasionally revises historical counts slightly downward or reclassifies deaths between the confirmed and suspected categories.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative combined measles death toll reported by Bangladesh's Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) in its daily measles bulletin covering the 24 hours ending 08:00 Bangladesh Standard Time (UTC+6) on 12 November 2026. The value is the cumulative total of measles-related deaths since 15 March 2026 stated in that bulletin — laboratory-confirmed measles deaths plus deaths among people with measles-like symptoms (suspected measles deaths) — not the number of new deaths reported for that 24-hour period. The figure is taken from The Business Standard's report of that bulletin, whose headline toll figure is the value to use, listed at https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/health; if The Business Standard does not report that bulletin, the cumulative total stated for 12 November 2026 is taken from other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Example: if the bulletin reports 1,318 cumulative confirmed-plus-suspected measles deaths, the question resolves to 1318.
question.fine_print: If DGHS publishes no bulletin covering the 24 hours ending 08:00 BST on 12 November 2026, the question resolves using the cumulative total in the next DGHS measles bulletin published before 19 November 2026; if no DGHS measles bulletin is published between 12 and 19 November 2026, the question is annulled.
